repairs.feedback:
A reviewer checked it against the person's conditions and found these not met:
- C-001: The automation reads every row with status 'new', not only website-form leads. The practice run routed Lou (source 'referral') and Ray (source 'event') as well as Pat (source 'website').
- C-006: The automation refers to Marcus only by name. It contains no marcus@sunrisesolar.energy address, and its assumptions state that no e-mail is sent.
- C-007: The automation refers to Priya only by name. It contains no priya@sunrisesolar.energy address, and no e-mail is sent.
- C-008: The default rule assigns leads to Priya by name, and the practice run confirms this. However, the automation does not include priya@sunrisesolar.energy as the destination address.
Fix the workflow so it meets them.

workflow.title: Route new website leads to Marcus or Priya and log assignments
workflow.goal: Route each new website-form lead (source 'website', status 'new'): companies over 200 employees go to Priya (priya@sunrisesolar.energy); otherwise leads in California go to Marcus (marcus@sunrisesolar.energy); all other website leads go to Priya. Record every assignment, with the assignee's address, in the lead-log sheet.

assumptions: Only leads with source 'website' and status 'new' are routed; referral, event, contacted and spam leads are skipped.
California is matched when region or country contains 'california', or region/country equals 'CA' (case-insensitive).
Assignee addresses are marcus@sunrisesolar.energy for Marcus and priya@sunrisesolar.energy for Priya; they are recorded in lead-log as the destination for each assignment.
No e-mail or chat is sent by this workflow; the assignment is recorded in lead-log only.
companySize is a number of employees; a lead with company size over 200 goes to Priya even if in California.
risks: assignedAt is not filled per row because no capability can stamp a per-row timestamp; the lead-log row has no assignment time.
A lead with a missing or non-numeric companySize will not match the size rule and falls through to the California or default rule.
Leads whose region or country is spelled differently (for example 'Calif.') will not be recognised as California.
Because no e-mail is sent, Marcus and Priya are not notified; they must read lead-log to see new assignments.
successCriteria: Every new website-form lead appears in lead-log exactly once with the assignee and assignee address chosen by the rules.
Referral and event leads are not routed or logged.
The appended row count matches the number of routed leads.
sheet.audit confirms the appended lead-log rows are present.

nodes.description: Read all rows of the leads sheet.
Keep only website-form leads with status new.
Label each website lead: size over 200 goes to Priya; California goes to Marcus; everyone else goes to Priya. Each assignee's address is set alongside the name.
Build lead-log rows with name, email, company, assignee and assignee address.
Append the assignments to the lead-log sheet.
Independently confirm the appended lead-log rows are in the sheet.

metadata.rationale: Filter to website-form leads first so other sources are ignored. Ordered rules keep the size rule ahead of the California rule. Each assignee's address is stored with the assignment so the destination is explicit in lead-log.
